resale_co.name: Residential Owner Certificate (Certificate of Occupancy before sale, also called Certificate of Continued Occupancy)
resale_co.lead_time: Standard inspection has no stated lead time; an expedited inspection (done within 3 business days) costs an extra $50
requirements: Purchaser fills out and signs the application with original signatures, notarized, plus a notarized affidavit stating the number of dwelling units and that they buy the property as is and are responsible for outstanding violations
LLC buyers or sellers must give the actual name of the manager or principal
Boilers and furnaces need a full fire rated ceiling or a sprinkler on the water line
All permits closed with final inspections done; no open building code or property maintenance violations
Exits clear; no padlocks or key locks on exit doors; no keyed locks on interior doors
Handrails on stairs with three or more risers
Working smoke and carbon monoxide detectors
Fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen, properly mounted and easy to reach
Windows open and have no broken or cracked glass
No trash or rubbish buildup inside or outside
Inspector must have access to all areas of the property

fees.label: Continued certificate of occupancy inspection, townhouse, condominium or one-family (Ord. 06-24, 2024)
Continued certificate of occupancy inspection, two-family house (Ord. 06-24, 2024)
Expedited inspection, completed within three business days, added to the fee above
fees.quote: (9) Expedited certificate of continued certificate of occupancy inspection fee (inspection completed within three business days) is $50, along with the fee referenced above.

fees.label: Re-inspection after a failed inspection, each time
fees.quote: Re-inspection fee for any of the above use groups [for any inspection that fails and requires additional inspection(s) to be performed] shall pay an additional $40 for each re-inspection conducted.

fees.label: Continued certificate of occupancy, any use group (separate line in the 2024 ordinance; unclear whether it is charged in addition to the inspection fee)
fees.quote: (d) The fee for a continued certificate of occupancy shall be $100 for any type of Use Group.

fees.label: Cancelling or rescheduling an inspection less than 24 hours ahead (Ord. 22-23, 2023)
fees.quote: A forty-dollar ($40) cancellation fee shall be assessed for each inspection cancelled or rescheduled less than twenty-four (24) hours in advance of such appointment.

resale_co.how_to_apply: The purchaser completes the Residential Owner Certificate application (page 1) and the Certification/Affidavit (page 2), both signed with original signatures and notarized, and files it with the Building Department, Town Hall, 6808 Park Avenue, Guttenberg, with a check or money order payable to Town of Guttenberg. The Building Department then inspects.
resale_co.contact_title: Technical Assistant to the Construction Official

resale_co.notes: Required by Town Code section 11-4.3 and 11-4.4 as amended by Ordinance 22-23 (adopted August 28, 2023): no one may occupy a building after a sale or change of ownership until the Construction Official, Fire Official or Fire Inspector issues a Certificate of Occupancy, and the purchaser must apply for a Residential Owner Certificate. Fees come from Ordinance 06-24 (adopted May 22, 2024), which restated the Building Department fee schedule; both ordinances are printed in full in the council minutes on the Town site. The 2023 ordinance and 2024 ordinance set the same one-family ($100) and two-family ($125) amounts. The October 2023 application lists $100.00 for condominium and co-op and $125.00 for a two unit dwelling but has no one-family line; it also shows the $40.00 reinspection fee as per unit. The Residential Owner Certificate application pages are scanned images read visually. The Construction Official's name was not found; the Building Department email in the Town directory belongs to Yomaris Alcantara, hired June 2025 as technical assistant to the Construction Official. The Town directory lists the Building Department at 201-868-2315, ext. 149, 106, 107 (data feed behind https://www.guttenbergnj.org/directory). Guttenberg also has a Residential Tenant Certificate for each change of tenants ($100) and short-term rental certificates; those are rental programs, not resale requirements.

requirements: All smoke detectors must be 10-year sealed units (since January 1, 2019)
Smoke detector on each level including the basement (not the attic or crawl space); smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm outside each sleeping area within 10 feet of bedrooms
Carbon monoxide alarms placed next to fuel burning equipment, and replaced if older than 8 to 10 years
All front doors leading to hallways must self-close
The July 2024 Town form still lists fire extinguishers mounted in the proper location (state law dropped the extinguisher in 2025)
Applications brought in after 12 noon count as the next business day

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for One, Two-Family Dwellings, Condominium, Co-op and Town House (Certification of Smoke Detector / Carbon Monoxide Alarm / Fire Extinguisher Compliance), check every box, and bring it to Guttenberg Fire Prevention, 6808 Park Avenue, with a check or money order payable to Town of Guttenberg. Credit cards are accepted with a surcharge. The application fee is not refunded.

fire_cert.notes: The Town is the local fire enforcing agency (DCA registry code M); fire fighting is by North Hudson Regional Fire and Rescue, but resale smoke/CO certificates are handled by the Town's Fire Prevention office. Fees come from the Town's July 2024 application (a scanned form read visually); the 2018 guidelines sheet lists the same $45.00 / $90.00 / $161.00 tiers. The Town reappointed Albert Salvesen as Fire Official for 2026. The form fax number (201-268-5309) differs from the guidelines sheet and state directory (201-868-5309).
